es.value: `__slots__` declara de antemano qué atributos puede tener una instancia. Ahorra memoria (no crea `__dict__`) y evita errores: asignar un atributo no declarado lanza `AttributeError`.
Útil cuando creas MUCHOS objetos iguales: el ahorro de memoria se nota.

en.value: `__slots__` declares in advance which attributes an instance may have. It saves memory (no `__dict__`) and prevents bugs: assigning an undeclared attribute raises `AttributeError`.
Handy when you create MANY identical objects: the memory saving adds up.

prompt.es: Define `Punto` con `__slots__ = ('x', 'y')` e `__init__(x, y)`. No debe tener `__dict__`.
prompt.en: Define `Punto` with `__slots__ = ('x', 'y')` and `__init__(x, y)`. It must not have `__dict__`.

tests.name: Punto
tests.harness:
p = Punto(1, 2)
assert (p.x, p.y) == (1, 2)
assert not hasattr(p, '__dict__')

prompt.es: Define `Punto3D` con `__slots__ = ('x', 'y', 'z')` e `__init__(x, y, z)`. Asignar un atributo fuera de slots debe dar AttributeError (lo comprueba el test).
prompt.en: Define `Punto3D` with `__slots__ = ('x', 'y', 'z')` and `__init__(x, y, z)`. Assigning an attribute outside slots must raise AttributeError (the test checks it).

es: Declara __slots__ = ('x', 'y', 'z') y asigna las tres en __init__.
en: Declare __slots__ = ('x', 'y', 'z') and assign all three in __init__.

tests.name: Punto3D
tests.harness:
p = Punto3D(1, 2, 3)
assert (p.x, p.y, p.z) == (1, 2, 3)
assert not hasattr(p, '__dict__')
err = False
try:
    p.w = 4
except AttributeError:
    err = True
assert err is True
